scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

prediction.raw: **YTA (Yes, You're the Asshole)** **Why:** - **You were legally and morally responsible** for your brother’s well-being while your mom was out. As the 18-year-old in charge, your primary duty was to enforce boundaries (like bedtime), not to prioritize your friend’s or your brother’s desires over his health. - **A 7-year-old cannot self-regulate sleep consequences**. While you claim "2 hours of missed sleep is not a big deal," research shows even small sleep disruptions severely impact children’s mood, cognitive function, and behavior. Your brother’s next-day crankiness proves it *was* a big deal. - **You abdicated responsibility** by deferring to your friend’s suggestion. As the adult in charge, *you* should have made the call to enforce bedtime, even if it meant handling a tantrum. "Dragging him upstairs" is part of the job— it’s not "embarrassing or exhausting" to do what’s necessary for a child’s safety and health. - **"Letting him learn consequences" is a harmful rationalization**. Children need consistent, adult-imposed boundaries to learn safely. Allowing him to stay up late *because* he might feel tired tomorrow is not "teaching responsibility"— it’s negligence. A 7-year-old lacks the maturity to understand or manage such consequences on their own. **What you should do:** Apologize to your mom, acknowledge your mistake, and commit to being firmer next time. Sleep is non-negotiable for young children, and as the responsible adult, you failed to prioritize it. **Final verdict: YTA** (1) *(Note: "YTA" = "Yes, You're the Asshole"— the standard AITA judgment for actions that are clearly unreasonable or harmful.)*

For a 7-year-old, even an hour or two can affect their mood and behavior. The next day's crankiness proves it was a problem. - As the person in charge, the user should have enforced bedtime. Even if the brother was resistant, it's his job to handle it. Dragging him up or dealing with a tantrum is part of being responsible. - The friend's opinion shouldn't override the user's duty. The user should have said no to the friend's suggestion and made the brother go back to bed. - The mom's expectation is that the user would ensure the brother gets proper sleep. By not doing so, the user failed in his responsibility. So, the user is likely the asshole here. AITA would be "YTA" (Yes, You're the Asshole) because he didn't fulfill his duty as the temporary guardian. Even though the brother is 7 and can put himself to bed, when he's awake and wants to stay up, the responsible adult should enforce the rules. But wait, the user mentioned "he can put himself to bed," but that doesn't mean he's responsible for his own sleep schedule when an adult is in charge. The adult is supposed to ensure he's in bed at the right time. Also, the user's argument that "he should know about consequences" is flawed. A 7-year-old doesn't fully grasp long-term consequences like adults do. They need consistent boundaries set by adults. Letting him stay up and then being cranky the next day is a consequence, but the user should have prevented it in the first place. So, the correct judgment is YTA. The user failed in his responsibility by not making the brother go back to bed, leading to the negative outcome. The mom's anger is justified.
